title: Impact of New Seed Variety Adoption on Farm Income

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The identification strategy employed in this analysis is Instrumental Variables (IV). The key assumption is that agroecological suitability (z) is a valid instrumental variable, meaning it affects the adoption of the new seed variety (x), but does not directly affect farm income (y) except through its effect on x. Additionally, the exclusion restriction assumes that z does not directly influence y, and the monotonicity assumption ensures that the effect of z on x is either positive or zero for all units.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(stargazer)
library(plm)

# Load the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s79_data.csv")

# Check the data structure
str(data)

# Run IV regression using 2SLS
iv_model <- plm(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data, model = "instrumental")

# Print the IV regression results
stargazer(iv_model, type = "latex")

# Basic robustness checks: Overidentification test
# Since we have only one instrument, we cannot perform an overidentification test.
# However, we can check the first-stage F-statistic to ensure it is not weak
summary(iv_model)

# We can also look at the reduced form to check the effect of z on y
reduced_form <- plm(y ~ z + controls, data = data, model = "lm")
stargazer(reduced_form, type = "latex")

# Check for potential issues like multicollinearity
vif <- function(x) {
  1 / (1 - (x ^ 2))
}
lm_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
vif_values <- vif(lm_model$r.squared)
print(paste("VIF:", vif_values))

```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient of x in the IV regression to be positive and statistically significant, indicating that the adoption of the new seed variety increases farm income. The magnitude of this effect will depend on the strength of the relationship between z and x, as well as between x and y. A stronger relationship between z and x (i.e., a higher first-stage F-statistic) will lead to more precise estimates of the effect of x on y. If the results are robust across different model specifications and robustness checks, this will provide evidence that the adoption of the new seed variety has a causal, positive effect on farm income. The expected magnitude of the effect will depend on the units of measurement of y and x; for example, if y is measured in dollars and x is a binary variable, a coefficient of x = 0.5 might indicate that adopting the new seed variety increases farm income by $500.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use agroecological suitability as an instrument for new seed variety adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Adopting the new seed variety leads to a significant increase in farm income.
